hints: Calculate the distance travelled in $8\text{ s}$ at constant speed $36\text{ m s}^{-1}$: $s = vt = 36 \times 8 = 288\text{ m}$.
Work done against the constant resistance force is $W = R \times s = 1250 \times 288\text{ J}$.
walkthrough:
State the formula for work done by a constant force along the line of motion:
$$W = F \times s$$

Find the distance $s$ travelled in $t = 8\text{ s}$ at constant speed $v = 36\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$s = vt = (36)(8) = 288\text{ m}$$

Multiply the constant resistance force $R = 1250\text{ N}$ by the distance:
$$W = (1250)(288) = 360000\text{ J} = 360\text{ kJ}$$
Thus the work done against the resisting force during the first $8$ seconds is $360\,000\text{ J}$ (or $360\text{ kJ}$).

hints: At constant speed on level ground, the engine driving force balances the resistance force: $F_D = 1250\text{ N}$.
Use $P = F_D v = 1250 \times 36\text{ W}$, then divide by $1000$ to give the power in kW.
walkthrough:
State the relationship for power developed by a driving force at instantaneous speed $v$:
$$P = F_D v$$

Because the car moves at constant speed on a horizontal road, the acceleration is zero ($a = 0$). By Newton's first law, the forward driving force balances the backward resisting force:
$$F_D = R = 1250\text{ N}$$

Substitute $F_D = 1250\text{ N}$ and $v = 36\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = (1250)(36) = 45000\text{ W}$$

Convert watts to kilowatts by dividing by $1000$:
$$P = \frac{45000}{1000} = 45\text{ kW}$$
Thus the power developed by the engine of the car is $45\text{ kW}$.

hints: The power is increased by $12\text{ kW}$, giving a new power of $45 + 12 = 57\text{ kW} = 57000\text{ W}$.
Find the new driving force at speed $36\text{ m s}^{-1}$: $F_D' = \frac{57000}{36}\text{ N}$.
Apply Newton's second law horizontally: $F_D' - 1250 = 1400a$, and solve for acceleration a.
walkthrough:
Calculate the new increased power developed by the engine:
$$P_{\text{new}} = 45\text{ kW} + 12\text{ kW} = 57\text{ kW} = 57000\text{ W}$$

Determine the new forward driving force $F_D'$ at instantaneous speed $v = 36\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D' = \frac{P_{\text{new}}}{v} = \frac{57000}{36} = \frac{4750}{3} \approx 1583.33\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law in the horizontal direction of motion:
$$\sum F = ma$$
$$F_D' - R = ma$$
Substitute the known values $F_D' = \frac{4750}{3}\text{ N}$, $R = 1250\text{ N}$, and $m = 1400\text{ kg}$:
$$\frac{4750}{3} - 1250 = 1400a$$
Express with a common denominator:
$$\frac{4750 - 3(1250)}{3} = 1400a$$
$$\frac{4750 - 3750}{3} = 1400a$$
$$\frac{1000}{3} = 1400a$$
Divide both sides by $1400$:
$$a = \frac{1000}{3 \times 1400} = \frac{1000}{4200} = \frac{5}{21} \approx 0.238095\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
Rounding to three significant figures gives:
$$a = 0.238\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
Thus the instantaneous acceleration of the car is $0.238\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

hints: Find the driving force from power and speed: $F_D = \frac{64000}{32} = 2000\text{ N}$.
At constant speed up the slope, driving force balances resistance plus the component of weight: $F_D = R + mg\sin\theta$.
Substitute $R = 1250\text{ N}$ and $mg = 14000\text{ N}$ to find $\sin\theta$, then calculate $\theta = \arcsin(\sin\theta)$.
walkthrough:
State the relationship connecting driving force, power, and speed:
$$P = F_D v$$
Substitute $P = 64\text{ kW} = 64000\text{ W}$ and constant speed $v = 32\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$64000 = F_D (32)$$
$$F_D = \frac{64000}{32} = 2000\text{ N}$$

Identify the forces acting on the car parallel to the inclined road:
- Forward driving force up the slope: $F_D = 2000\text{ N}$
- Constant resistance opposing motion down the slope: $R = 1250\text{ N}$
- Downward component of weight along the slope: $W_{\parallel} = mg\sin\theta = (1400)(10)\sin\theta = 14000\sin\theta$

Because the speed is constant, the acceleration is zero ($a = 0$). Equate the forward force to the total retarding force:
$$F_D = R + mg\sin\theta$$
$$2000 = 1250 + 14000\sin\theta$$
Subtract $1250$ from both sides:
$$750 = 14000\sin\theta$$
Divide both sides by $14000$:
$$\sin\theta = \frac{750}{14000} = \frac{75}{1400} = \frac{3}{56} \approx 0.0535714$$

Take the inverse sine:
$$\theta = \arcsin(0.0535714) \approx 3.0708^\circ$$
Rounding to one decimal place gives:
$$\theta = 3.1^\circ$$
Thus the angle of inclination of the road is $3.1^\circ$.
